The framework generates stances, reasons, debate arguments, and final judgments (label and justification) for hate speech detection through multi-agent interaction.

changes_made.explanation: Removed 'Dialogue Generation' as it's not accurate - the paper focuses on debate simulation for classification, not conversational dialogue. Simplified 'Other:Explanation Generation' to match formatting. Normalized model name to standard form. Refined output descriptions to be more precise.

'standard deviation' is not an evaluation metric but rather a measure of variability, so it was removed. The paper uses Accuracy and Fleiss' Kappa to evaluate the consistency and performance of the framework.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated methods descriptions into a single clear description. Added specific criteria mentioned in the paper about what the judge evaluates. Normalized model naming.
No human evaluation was conducted in this paper - all evaluations were automatic using metrics.

overall_notes: This paper presents PREDICT, a multi-agent debate framework for hate speech detection. While it uses LLMs to generate text (stances, reasons, arguments), the primary task is classification rather than NLG evaluation. The NLG aspects are in service of the classification task through debate simulation. The paper uses automatic evaluation metrics rather than focusing on NLG quality assessment.
